source_anchor.analysis_method: GitHub connector source inspection plus comparison with the supplied 2026-07-31 portability bundle

findings.observation: Development workspace and control-plane roots are encoded as %LOCALAPPDATA%\CanDoItAll\...
findings.risk: Linux and macOS receive unresolved or semantically invalid roots before deeper portability work can even be exercised.
findings.direction: Introduce portable root defaults and explicit legacy Windows token compatibility; remove host-specific roots from shared development configuration.

findings.observation: Infrastructure policies only replace Path.AltDirectorySeparatorChar while the MAF policy explicitly converts backslash. These produce different meanings on Unix.
findings.risk: A persisted logical locator can resolve differently depending on the caller, causing inaccessible artifacts, duplicate records, or containment defects.
findings.direction: Define one logical-path contract with '/' serialization and field-specific legacy backslash readers; keep physical path parsing separate.

findings.observation: Containment and root de-duplication use OrdinalIgnoreCase on every operating system.
findings.risk: Case-sensitive filesystems can treat distinct paths as equivalent in policy while the OS treats them as different.
findings.direction: Use logical ordinal semantics and root-specific physical filesystem semantics; add actual Linux/macOS characterization.

findings.observation: External-target aliases are shaped around Windows drive letters.
findings.risk: Unix absolute roots cannot be represented consistently and migration between hosts becomes ambiguous.
findings.direction: Version a platform-neutral alias format that identifies an allowed root without embedding drive-letter assumptions.

findings.observation: Routes, logical locators, physical paths, executable paths, and command text are often represented as plain strings with local normalization.
findings.risk: A broad separator replacement can corrupt URLs, Unix filenames containing backslash, or intentionally host-bound paths.
findings.direction: Inventory and classify every persisted and runtime path-bearing field before implementation; apply transformations only by field type.

findings.observation: Many sets, locks, and path comparisons use OrdinalIgnoreCase globally, while some use OperatingSystem.IsWindows as a proxy for filesystem behavior.
findings.risk: macOS can be case-sensitive or case-insensitive by volume, and Linux paths can collide in application state despite being distinct on disk.
findings.direction: Use ordinal semantics for logical identifiers and a root/volume-specific physical path policy for filesystem equality.

findings.observation: Filesystem enumeration is not uniformly ordered before producing persistent or decision-bearing results.
findings.risk: Linux, Windows, and macOS may return different order, changing plans, fingerprints, receipts, tests, or agent context.
findings.direction: Order by normalized logical key with an explicit comparer at every decision or persistence boundary.

findings.observation: Existing reparse checks are valuable but duplicated and do not constitute a proven race-resistant cross-platform contract.
findings.risk: A symlink swap or inconsistent check can escape trusted roots during read, write, open, or process execution.
findings.direction: Define one deny-by-default managed-root link policy, validate existing ancestors immediately before access, and document residual TOCTOU limits.

findings.observation: Several writes are direct, while other writes use temporary files with only in-process coordination.
findings.risk: Crashes or concurrent processes can leave truncated catalog, secret, or artifact state.
findings.direction: Centralize same-volume temporary write, flush, atomic replace, bounded cross-process lock, and recovery rules.

findings.observation: Filename sanitization depends on Path.GetInvalidFileNameChars, which is platform-specific.
findings.risk: The same artifact name can serialize to different physical names on different hosts or remain invalid after transfer.
findings.direction: Define an application-level portable filename policy and preserve the original display name separately.

findings.observation: No explicit 0700/0600 policy is applied to control-plane, key-ring, vault-key, or secret files.
findings.risk: Default umask and service-account configuration can expose protected local state to other users.
findings.direction: Apply and verify restrictive Unix modes after creation and migration; fail closed for secret-bearing state that cannot be hardened.

findings.observation: FileSystemWatcher errors schedule a rebuild, but there is no unified generation/fingerprint/rescan contract.
findings.risk: Overflow, coalescing, rename behavior, or platform differences can silently miss changes.
findings.direction: Treat watchers as hints, debounce by generation, and confirm state through deterministic rescan/fingerprint with polling fallback.

findings.observation: Absolute workspace roots and preferred executable paths are persisted without platform/host affinity or rebind state.
findings.risk: A profile copied to another OS can reinterpret a Windows path as a relative Unix name or silently select the wrong storage/application.
findings.direction: Version host-bound path records, detect foreign syntax, mark unresolved, and require explicit rebind or migration.

findings.observation: Default roots rely on LocalApplicationData/fallback behavior without an explicit Windows/Linux/macOS data/config/state policy.
findings.risk: Interactive, service, and headless deployments can place mutable or secret data in surprising locations.
findings.direction: Define explicit platform defaults, service overrides, path purpose, ownership, and migration behavior.

findings.observation: Auto selects MacOsKeychain on macOS and LinuxSecretService on Linux, but both are UnsupportedSecretVault implementations.
findings.risk: Startup may appear healthy while the first secret operation fails, blocking providers, storage, MCP, and plugins.
findings.direction: Implement and prove each advertised provider or make capability selection fail fast with actionable diagnostics.

findings.observation: DataProtectionFileVault creates a random AES key and writes it as plaintext Base64 beside the ciphertext.
findings.risk: Copying or reading the vault directory reveals both ciphertext and its decrypting key; the name overstates protection.
findings.direction: Remove it from production Auto, require an externally protected wrapping key or an OS/remote vault, and preserve only an explicit test/development mode.

findings.observation: ASP.NET Data Protection keys are persisted to the filesystem without an explicit cross-platform at-rest protector.
findings.risk: Legacy secret records and control-plane database passwords depend on key files whose confidentiality is not protected by the current configuration.
findings.direction: Bootstrap key-ring protection independently of the ring itself; support DPAPI on Windows and explicit secure macOS/Linux/headless strategies.

findings.observation: Three persistence mechanisms coexist: legacy Data Protection secret payloads, control-plane Data Protection passwords, and new vault references.
findings.risk: Changing one key location/provider can make the other two unreadable or create partial migrations.
findings.direction: Create an explicit migration state machine with source-side decryption, staged destination writes, verification, rollback, and per-record versioning.

findings.observation: Vault key/payload writes lack a unified atomic, permission, cross-process, rotation, and repair contract.
findings.risk: Concurrent startup or crash can produce mismatched key/payload generations.
findings.direction: Use versioned envelopes, atomic commits, bounded locks, restrictive modes, rotation checkpoints, and explicit recovery tooling.

findings.observation: Current runtime selection can register a nominal provider that is not operational on the host.
findings.risk: Feature UI and readiness can claim support that will fail only during work execution.
findings.direction: Perform startup capability probes for mandatory providers and expose bounded, non-secret readiness diagnostics for optional features.

findings.observation: Platform checks are distributed, but a single broad platform service would also violate current ownership boundaries.
findings.risk: Either branch sprawl or a god abstraction can couple unrelated modules and make testing harder.
findings.direction: Use small purpose-owned ports and leaf adapters selected at composition; common code continues using cross-platform .NET APIs directly.

findings.observation: The only discovered CI workflow is disabled. Its main application build/test runs only on Windows.
findings.risk: Cross-platform regressions and even general development regressions can merge without an active repository gate.
findings.direction: Restore an active workflow with Windows, Ubuntu, and macOS restore/build/stable-test gates plus targeted runtime proofs.

findings.observation: The installed-web-app path is Windows/PowerShell oriented.
findings.risk: Linux/macOS support remains a developer-only claim with no repeatable service/install/runbook path.
findings.direction: Retain the Windows installer, add Unix publish/service scripts or a small cross-platform installer boundary, and document service-user paths and rollback.

findings.observation: The central workspace host already uses typed argv and cross-platform ProcessStartInfo, but Unix process-group, signal, and tree-kill behavior is not proven.
findings.risk: Timeouts may leave grandchildren running or terminate incompletely.
findings.direction: Characterize Kill(entireProcessTree), cancellation, and stream drain on all target OSes before adding a purpose-specific native adapter.

findings.observation: The inherited allowlist is Windows-heavy and stored in an OrdinalIgnoreCase dictionary on every OS.
findings.risk: Unix variables can be dropped or case-collapsed, while Windows-only variables are treated as universal.
findings.direction: Separate safe common variables from OS/tool profiles and preserve host environment key semantics.

findings.observation: Two resolvers have different suffix and fallback rules; the workspace locator probes Windows suffixes on Unix.
findings.risk: The same capability can resolve differently in MCP, workspace tools, plugins, and Workbench.
findings.direction: Create one pure candidate/resolution contract with OS-specific leaf rules, execute-bit checks, stable diagnostics, and no implicit shell.

findings.observation: Runtime availability is Windows-only and every .NET, Docker, Conda, Python, or script plan is rendered as PowerShell text launched through powershell.exe/runas.
findings.risk: Unix hosts cannot launch runtime nodes, and ordinary direct commands inherit shell quoting/injection and presentation coupling.
findings.direction: Compile typed executable/argv/environment plans; execute directly; treat explicit shell scripts and optional terminal presentation as separate capabilities.

findings.observation: Virtual environments assume Scripts/Activate.ps1.
findings.risk: Linux/macOS virtual environments use different layouts and do not require activation for deterministic execution.
findings.direction: Resolve and invoke the environment interpreter directly; keep activation only as optional terminal display behavior.

findings.observation: Elevation is modeled as Windows runas.
findings.risk: Mapping this automatically to sudo/pkexec would create a privilege-escalation and interactive-hang risk.
findings.direction: Make elevation a separate optional capability that is unavailable by default on Unix/macOS unless an explicitly governed adapter is configured.

findings.observation: Windows discovery uses WMI command lines; Unix fallback only searches process name and often lacks command-line identity.
findings.risk: Recovery/cleanup can miss owned processes or terminate an unrelated process with the same name.
findings.direction: Persist launched-process identity first, then use OS-specific discovery as a bounded recovery aid with PID/start-time/user/executable/command/workspace proof.

findings.observation: System.Management and WMI behavior live in the general Manager project.
findings.risk: Windows-only implementation details remain easy to call from neutral code and complicate platform analysis.
findings.direction: Move WMI behind a Windows-only leaf adapter/registration boundary; keep the Manager contract neutral.

findings.observation: Allowed names and executable discovery use separate case/suffix models.
findings.risk: A command can pass the allowlist but resolve unexpectedly, or be rejected on one OS despite an equivalent installed executable.
findings.direction: Validate the resolved executable identity against a capability-owned allowlist using host-appropriate rules.

findings.observation: Resolver recursively scans a global npx cache and chooses the most recently written cli.js.
findings.risk: Selection is nondeterministic and can cross workspace/user trust boundaries.
findings.direction: Use a controlled, versioned application tool root with explicit integrity/version evidence; do not depend on global cache discovery for production.

findings.observation: External tools implement an independent local runner with distinct timeout, output, and kill behavior.
findings.risk: Security and portability fixes can land in one runner but not the other.
findings.direction: Reuse one execution primitive or explicitly prove why a separate boundary is required; share tested low-level process semantics.

findings.observation: External process stdout/stderr and environment bindings can flow into diagnostic messages.
findings.risk: Secrets or sensitive local paths can be captured in receipts, CI logs, or agent context.
findings.direction: Persist only approved environment names, cap/redact output, and route secret values through the runtime secret boundary.

findings.observation: The Docker plugin constructs LocalWorkspaceProcessHost directly and maintains its own executable/environment policy.
findings.risk: It bypasses owned process registries, composition-selected adapters, and later portability fixes.
findings.direction: Inject the authoritative host execution port, capability probe, and environment policy.

findings.observation: Desktop launch behavior is owned by package 0.1.18 outside this repository.
findings.risk: The main application can claim macOS/Linux support without package/runtime evidence.
findings.direction: Run a pinned compatibility matrix, record package capabilities, and fail closed or quarantine desktop launch when the package lacks a supported adapter.

findings.observation: The current refactor intentionally moved process semantics and recovery to Processes.
findings.risk: A generic OS-service refactor inside MAF or Infrastructure could reintroduce reverse ownership and duplicate domain policy.
findings.direction: Expose narrow host capabilities at execution boundaries; let Processes own eligibility, strategy, recovery, evidence, and domain failure semantics.

findings.observation: ProcessDriverLayer.Platform exists and could be misread as a generic OS abstraction layer.
findings.risk: Host implementation facts become process-domain truth or vice versa.
findings.direction: Use the layer only for process strategy packages that require declared host capabilities; do not move filesystem/secrets/process primitives into process drivers.

findings.observation: There is no active Windows/Linux/macOS runtime-node, Manager, MCP, or plugin proof.
findings.risk: A successful neutral build can mask runtime-only failures in process, terminal, desktop, or secret integration.
findings.direction: Add focused actual-host tests and failure injection after the core portability gate lands.

findings.observation: Projects target neutral net10.0 and the central workspace process host already uses direct typed arguments.
findings.risk: None; this reduces required rewrite scope.
findings.direction: Preserve and extend these foundations rather than replacing them with a new parallel runtime.

findings.observation: Recent refactors created clearer process, runtime, and security boundaries.
findings.risk: Portability changes could accidentally collapse these new boundaries.
findings.direction: Treat the latest architecture as authoritative and add portability through purpose-owned adapters.
